question:
An 79-year-old male presents one day after experiencing an episode of speech arrest, facial numbness
and weakness, and left arm weakness. The episode lasted about 60 minutes and resolved completely.
His medical history includes hypertension and hypercholesterolemia. On examination, his blood
pressure is 199/97 mm Hg, and his pulse is 75 beats per minute. Pulses in the distal extremities are
diminished. Neurologic examination reveals no abnormalities. No carotid bruits or cardiac murmurs are
detected. What is the most appropriate next step in evaluating this patient? Answer Choices: (A)
24-hour Holter monitoring (B) MRI and MR angiography of the head and neck (C) Transthoracic
echocardiography (D) Complete blood count and coagulation profile (E) Transthoracic echocardiogram
(F) CT perfusion scan of the brain (G) CT angiography of the head and neck (H) Electroencephalogram
(EEG) (I) Carotid Doppler ultrasonography (J) Urgent neurology consultation
 A. CT perfusion scan of the brain
B. 24-hour Holter monitoring
C. Transthoracic echocardiography
D. Transthoracic echocardiogram
E. CT angiography of the head and neck
F. Urgent neurology consultation
G. Complete blood count and coagulation profile
H. Electroencephalogram (EEG)
I. Carotid Doppler ultrasonography
J. MRI and MR angiography of the head and neck
